intuition.title: Surface area and reaction completion
intuition.text: The authors link the greater reactivity of nano-Al to its high surface area. Nano-Al converts fully under their 1000–1100 °C conditions, while coarse commercial feedstocks retain local excess Al even when powder XRD shows only AlN reflections. The smaller feedstock does not imply that its original size survives: partially reacted Al/AlN droplets are 5–15 µm.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Nitridation, footnote 11 and partial-reaction discussion

intuition.title: AlCl3 as a proposed vapor-transport reagent
intuition.text: AlCl3 addition favors whisker growth and changes partially reacted droplet shapes. The proposed Figure 2 transport cycle involves volatile AlCl and AlCl3, with AlN deposition from vapor. These transient species and reaction pathways are proposed from morphology and cited equilibria, not directly measured intermediates.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 2 and vapor-transport discussion

intuition.title: Heating rate changes the reaction history
intuition.text: Rapid heating is proposed to reduce the time available for Al particles to coalesce and for AlCl3 to sublime away before nitridation begins. The source places reaction onset around 1073 K, about 140 K above Al melting. This mechanistic onset is not a new specimen-specific synthesis schedule.

intuition.title: Why the authors favor vapor–solid growth
intuition.text: No flux droplets were seen at whisker tips, unspecified potential flux materials did not promote whiskers, and diverse branching directions were observed. These observations favor the authors’ vapor–solid interpretation over vapor–liquid–solid growth; they do not identify every unseen intermediate or provide a tested list of flux reagents.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Whisker-growth mechanism discussion

intuition.title: Measured geometry, a model input and size ranges
intuition.text: The 40–180 nm Scherrer range, 10–200 nm TEM crystallites and 0.5–5 µm aggregates describe different bases in the nano-Al series. Footnote 6 separately labels a 28 nm analytical input. A 44 nm input appears in a Kelvin-equation argument predicting only a 2–3% equilibrium vapor-pressure increase; it is not a new synthetic specimen. The authors instead propose enhanced nonequilibrium steady-state vapor pressure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Nano-Al characterization, footnote 6 and Kelvin discussion

intuition.title: Whiskers versus polycrystalline fibers
intuition.text: SAD establishes single crystallinity for the examined whiskers; study-wide whisker diameters are generally 20–100 nm with aspect ratios 20 to greater than 100. SEM alone cannot establish whether the stubble on partially nitrided Al droplets is single-crystal whiskers. TEM fragments show that some similar material is polycrystalline fibers. These observations remain separate rather than relabeling all fibers as whiskers.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Whisker dimensions, partial-reaction discussion and footnote 14

intuition.title: Scope of practical implications
intuition.text: The paper demonstrates morphological control by varying feed size, chloride addition and ramp rate. It does not measure device, thermal, optical or mechanical performance of the resulting particles. The precursor preparation also has a source-reported explosion warning; the referenced six-page SI with detailed precautions and synthetic procedures remains unreviewed.

general_background.title: Thermodynamics and kinetics
general_background.summary: Thermodynamics describes which states are energetically favoured, while kinetics governs how quickly a system can move between them. A change can be favourable yet proceed slowly when an activation barrier or limited transport restricts the pathway.
